functionality.rationale: Identity creation or pairing-record failures can permanently lose trust state or disable pairing.

security.rationale: Private keys and trust records must never fall back to plaintext, synchronized, or attacker-controlled storage.

performance.rationale: Protected-store access occurs on startup and trust updates but must not stall runtime state ownership.

compatibility.rationale: Stored identity and pairing records must remain readable or fail closed across supported upgrades.

concurrency.rationale: Concurrent first-run identity creation and trust updates must be atomic and race-safe.

platform.rationale: Keychain, Credential Manager, and Secret Service have different protection and availability semantics.

persistence.rationale: This task owns durable private identity and peer trust records, including corruption and rollback behavior.

adr.rationale: Protected identity and pairing records introduce a persisted security-sensitive format.

architecture.rationale: ADR 0006 owns the durable provider boundary; this task implements it.

roadmap.rationale: Protected storage is a pairing prerequisite, not a complete P1 milestone.
